topic: Large Language Models and the Transformer Architecture
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of computer science

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Vector Space Concept
lecture_lines: Computers represent words as lists of numbers.
These are vectors in a multi-dimensional space.
Similar words cluster together in this space.
animations: Visualize a list of numbers representing the word 'King' using #FF5733 text color.
Display a 3D coordinate system (background #000000) showing vector arrows pointing to points in space.
Highlight the 'King' and 'Queen' clusters in the vector space using #33FF57 circles.

sections.title: The Core Problem: Contextual Ambiguity
lecture_lines: Traditional models read sequences one by one.
They often lose context for long sentences.
Attention lets models look at all parts.
animations: Show a serial reading of words one by one in #FFFFFF.
Fade out the earlier words to represent memory loss.
Display a glowing network connecting all words simultaneously in #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Transformer: The 'Attention' Mechanism
lecture_lines: Self-attention acts like a dynamic spotlight.
Every word weighs its focus on others.
The mechanism uses Query and Key vectors.
Meaning changes based on context weights.
animations: Represent a spotlight moving across a sentence in #FFFF00.
Show lines connecting a central word to others with weights #33FF57.
Visualize Query, Key, and Value vectors as distinct colored bars (#3357FF, #FF33A1, #FF9933).
Show the Softmax function mapping weights to a probability distribution.
Update the word representation based on the calculated attention weights.

sections.title: Scaling Up: Why 'Large' Matters
lecture_lines: LLMs are Transformers scaled to massive sizes.
They contain billions of internal parameters.
Scale creates nuanced human language maps.
animations: Show a small model scaling up to a massive network in #FFFFFF.
Visualize billions of parameters as a dense grid of points.
Highlight a complex, nuanced path within the mapped parameter space.

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: Vectors, Attention, and Scale work together.
It generates text by traversing space.
animations: Display the three concepts (Vectors, Attention, Scale) merging into one.
Show a probability bar graph evolving with each generated word.
Trace a path through the vector space representing generated text.
